overview:
The target is a deterministic Turing machine, with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of tapes, that multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa = 2^{-182}$. This disproves the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) that $n\log n$ is the best possible in the [fixed-tape model](machine-model.md). The result is stated in [Power-saving integer multiplication](main-result.md).

The wiki starts with the model and the conjecture, then builds the Fourier tools. [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) is turned into pointwise multiplication by the [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md), which [butterflies](butterfly.md) compute in $\log t$ layers. The [synthetic transform](synthetic-transform.md) works over the ring modulo $y^r+1$ ([ring-y](ring-y.md)), where twiddle factors are signed shifts.

The saving comes from the tape. After the [stream operations](stream-ops.md) and [controlled shifts](controlled-shifts.md), the wiki builds [frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md) and [nested subspace labels](subspace-labels.md). The [recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md) then makes [address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) and the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) cost the volume times a power below one of their width. These give the [tape layout for synthetic transforms](transform-layout.md) and [ring convolution](ring-convolution.md).

Prime-length transforms are reduced to power-of-two ones by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) and the [Bluestein chirp](chirp.md), and the [Chinese-remainder address map](crt-map.md) places the convolution on prime axes. The [multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md) chains these steps, [error tracking](precision-recovery.md) shows that rounding recovers exact integers, and [cost accounting](cost-accounting.md) gives the exponent $\kappa$.

parts.title: Model and Conjecture
parts.intro: This part fixes the computation model of the main theorem, a Turing machine with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of tapes whose heads move one cell per step. It then states the [Schönhage–Strassen optimality conjecture](conjecture.md) that the result disproves. Every cost bound later in the wiki is a statement about this model.

parts.title: Convolution and Fourier Tools
parts.intro: Multiplying integers reduces to [cyclic convolution](convolution.md), and the [discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) turns convolution into a pointwise product. This part covers [butterflies](butterfly.md), [multidimensional transforms](multidim-transform.md), the [ring modulo $y^r+1$](ring-y.md) with its [synthetic transform](synthetic-transform.md), [contractions](contraction-maps.md) for bounding error, and [fixed-point records](fixed-point.md) for storing complex values. The later tape and error arguments assume all of these.

parts.title: Linear Operations on Tape
parts.intro: This part shows what a machine with a few tapes can do in time linear in the array volume. [Stream operations](stream-ops.md) give scans, splits and merges, [controlled shifts](controlled-shifts.md) update an address field by a computed offset, and the [matrix shear](matrix-shear.md) uses a triangular factorization to do a shear with few field interchanges. The tape procedures in the next parts are assembled from these.

parts.title: Frames and Rank Deficit
parts.intro: This part develops the abstract source of the power saving. A [linear exchange network](exchange-network.md) with restored scratch wires, [frames on wire arrays](array-frames.md), [tensor products of subspaces](tensor-product-of-spaces.md) and [nested subspace labels](subspace-labels.md) show that a call at parameter $mf$ needs only $s<Wm$ smaller calls. The [recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md) turns that count into a cost bound.

parts.title: Fast Tape Primitives
parts.intro: This part applies the recursion to the two tape procedures the algorithm needs. The [address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md) and [packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md) move and combine address fields. The [two-point kernel](phase-kernel.md) and [binary phase frames](phase-frames.md) give the [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md) that does several transform layers at once.

parts.title: Synthetic Transforms on Tape
parts.intro: This part puts the fast primitives to work on ring convolution. The [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md) avoids reordering, and the [tape layout](transform-layout.md) makes each transform round one simultaneous layer. The [established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier](hvdh-multiplier.md) and [signed packing](signed-packing.md) handle the pointwise polynomial products, which gives [ring convolution](ring-convolution.md).

parts.title: Prime Lengths and Address Maps
parts.intro: The integer product needs Fourier transforms of pairwise coprime prime lengths, but the fast transform handles powers of two. This part covers the [Bluestein chirp](chirp.md), [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) and [retained permutation cancellation](retained-permutations.md), which together avoid executing any sort. It also covers the [Chinese-remainder address map](crt-map.md) that places a long convolution on prime axes.

parts.title: Multiplication and Cost
parts.intro: This part assembles the algorithm. [Radix digits](radix-digit-reduction.md), the [phase twist](phase-twist.md), the [parameter choice](parameter-choice.md) and [error tracking](precision-recovery.md) feed the [multiplication algorithm](multiplication-algorithm.md). [Cost accounting](cost-accounting.md) then gives the exponent $\kappa$, which yields the [main result](main-result.md).
